# API Reference

This document is a reference for the Crux API. It contains information about the different APIs, the resources they return, and the response objects. Refer to the [intro](/docs/api-documentation/intro.md) for more information about the API or the [authentication](/docs/api-documentation/authentication.md) page for information about how to authenticate your API requests.

<!-- BEGIN AUTOGENERATED API ENDPOINTS -->

## API Endpoints

### `POST /api/v1/climbs/:id/comments`

> Posts a comment on a climb, the same as commenting in the app: it shows in the climb's activity and notifies anyone it mentions and, on a custom climb, the climb's poster. Comments are text only; photos and videos aren't supported yet. Returns the new comment with a 201 status.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the climb to comment on. A merged climb's ID (a copy made to climb it at another angle) comments on the climb it was merged into. This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `body`
> 
> The text of the comment, up to 2500 characters. Mention a user with `@[username:ID]`, as the app does. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Any authenticated user; the comment is posted as you. Climbs you can't see (other people's drafts) return a 404.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [ClimbComment](#climbcomment)
> 

### `GET /api/v1/gyms/:gym_slug/climb_lists`

> Returns all public climb lists for a specific gym.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `gym_slug`
> 
> The URL slug of the gym whose lists you want to retrieve. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Public.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [ClimbList](#climblist)
> 

### `GET /api/v1/users/:user_id/climb_lists`

> Returns all climb lists created by a user.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `user_id`
> 
> Must be "me" or your own user ID, since you can only view your own lists. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> You can only view your own lists.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [ClimbList](#climblist)
> 

### `GET /api/v1/climb_lists/:id`

> Returns details for a specific climb list. Must be public or owned by the user.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the climb list to retrieve. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Public if the list is public. Otherwise, restricted to the user who owns the list.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [ClimbList (full)](#climblist-full)
> 

### `POST /api/v1/climb_lists/:list_id/add_climb`

> Adds a climb to a climb list. Returns HTTP 200 if successful.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `list_id`
> 
> The ID of the list to add the climb to. This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `climb_id`
> 
> The ID of the climb to add. A merged climb's ID (a copy made to climb it at another angle) adds the climb it was merged into. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> User must own the list or be a gym admin of a gym-owned list. A gym admin editing the gym's list needs the gym's plan to include the public API (Crux Pro); otherwise returns a 403.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [Empty](#empty)
> 

### `POST /api/v1/climb_lists/:list_id/remove_climb`

> Removes a climb from a list. Returns HTTP 200 if successful.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `list_id`
> 
> The ID of the list. This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `climb_id`
> 
> The ID of the climb to remove. A merged climb's ID (a copy made to climb it at another angle) removes the climb it was merged into. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> User must own the list or be a gym admin of a gym-owned list. A gym admin editing the gym's list needs the gym's plan to include the public API (Crux Pro); otherwise returns a 403.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [Empty](#empty)
> 

### `GET /api/v1/climbs/:id`

> Returns details for a specific climb, including drafts (which the gym climb lists leave out), so a climb returned as a wall's active climb can always be fetched. The ID of a climb that was merged into another (a copy made to climb it at another angle) returns the climb it was merged into, whose `id` differs from the one requested.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the climb to retrieve. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Public.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [Climb (full)](#climb-full)
>

### `POST /api/v1/climbs/:id/activate`

> Sets a climb as the active climb on its wall. Only one climb can be active per gym, so any other active climb at the gym is deactivated. The climb is deactivated automatically 2 hours after it was activated (activating it again restarts the 2 hours). Triggers the `climb.activated` webhook, and `climb.deactivated` for any climb it replaces and when it times out. Returns the activated climb.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the climb to set as active. A merged climb's ID acts on the climb it was merged into. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Any authenticated user. The climb's gym must have LED features enabled.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [Climb (full)](#climb-full)
> 

### `POST /api/v1/climbs/:id/deactivate`

> Clears the active climb on the climb's wall, if this climb is the active one. Does nothing if the climb is not currently active. Triggers the `climb.deactivated` webhook when it clears the climb. Returns HTTP 200 if successful.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the climb to deactivate. A merged climb's ID acts on the climb it was merged into. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Any authenticated user. The climb's gym must have LED features enabled.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [Empty](#empty)
>

> #### Parameters:

### `GET /api/v1/gym_walls/:id/holds`

> Returns the holds on a gym wall's current photo, with the photo they're on. Hold masks are in the photo's `width` x `height` pixels. This is the same as `GET /api/v1/wall_photos/:id/holds` for the wall's current photo.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the gym wall whose holds you want to retrieve. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Public.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [WallPhoto (with_holds)](#wallphoto-with_holds)
> 

### `POST /api/v1/gym_walls/:id/climbs`

> Creates a climb on a gym wall from holds on the wall's photo, picked by their IDs from `GET /api/v1/gym_walls/:id/holds`. Crux draws the climb's image for you, the same way it draws climbs posted in the app. Send the parameters as a JSON body. Triggers the same webhooks as posting a climb in the app. Returns the new climb with a 201 status. If any hold IDs aren't on the photo, returns a 422 with the unknown IDs in `unknown_hold_ids`.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the gym wall to create the climb on. This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `name`
> 
> The name of the climb. This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `grade`
> 
> The grade of the climb. Must be one of the gym's grades (see `GET /api/v1/gyms/:gym_slug`). This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `holds`
> 
> The holds in the climb, as a list of `{ "id": "...", "type": "start" }` objects. `id` is a hold ID from the photo's holds. `type` is one of [hand, hand_l, hand_r, foot, foot_l, foot_r, start, finish, zone]. Optionally add `circuit_numbers`, a list of integers, to put a hold in a circuit. This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `photo_id`
> 
> The ID of the wall photo the holds are on (defaults to the wall's current photo). Must be a photo of this wall. This parameter is optional.
> 
> ##### `description`
> 
> A description of the climb. This parameter is optional.
> 
> ##### `foot_rules`
> 
> The climb's foot rules, as returned in a climb's `foot_rules` (for example `feet_follow_hands`). Leave it out for the standard rules. This parameter is optional.
> 
> ##### `no_matching`
> 
> Set to `true` if hands can't match on any hold except the start and finish holds, or `false` if they can. Defaults to the gym's setting for new climbs (usually `false`). This parameter is optional.
> 
> ##### `angle`
> 
> The wall angle the climb is set (and graded) at, in positive degrees past vertical: 0 is vertical, 40 is a 40° overhang. For walls with an adjustable angle; use one of the wall's `angles`. Climbers can then climb it at any of the wall's angles. This parameter is optional.
> 
> ##### `draft`
> 
> Set to `true` to save the climb as a draft, visible only to you. Defaults to `false`. This parameter is optional.
> 
> ##### `official`
> 
> Set to `true` to create an official climb instead of a custom climb. Requires `color`. This parameter is optional.
> 
> ##### `color`
> 
> The climb's hold color, for official climbs. Must be one of the gym's hold colors. This parameter is optional.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Any authenticated user can create custom climbs; the climb is posted as you. Official climbs can only be created by the gym's admins, and only when the gym's plan includes the public API (Crux Pro; otherwise a 403). Free-tier gyms limit how many climbs you can create, the same as in the app. A gym that switched off "Climbers can post climbs on photos" only takes climbers' climbs on its spray walls.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [Climb (full)](#climb-full)
>

### `POST /api/v1/climbs/:id/sends`

> Logs a send of a climb for you, the same as logging it in the app: it goes in your climb session at the climb's gym on `send_date` (created if needed) and triggers the `climb.sent` webhooks. A send of a climb you've already sent is a repeat. To import a climber's history, log their sends oldest first, so each climb's first send is the one that isn't a repeat. Returns the new send with a 201 status.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the climb you sent. The ID of a climb that was merged into another (a copy made to climb it at another angle) logs the send on the climb it was merged into, at the copy's angle unless `angle` is given. This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `send_date`
> 
> The date you sent it on, in your own time zone (YYYY-MM-DD). Can be in the past, not in the future. This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `attempts`
> 
> How many attempts the send took, from 1 (a flash) to 100. Defaults to the attempts you've already logged towards it in the app, or 1. This parameter is optional.
> 
> ##### `angle`
> 
> The angle you climbed it at, in positive degrees past vertical (0 is vertical, 40 is a 40° overhang): one of the climb's wall's `angles`. Only for climbs on walls with an adjustable angle, where it defaults to the climb's set `angle`; an angle the wall doesn't support returns a 422. Ignored for other climbs. On an adjustable wall, sends and attempts count per angle: your first send at each angle isn't a repeat, and `attempts` defaults to the attempts you've logged at that angle. This parameter is optional.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Any authenticated user; the send is logged as you. Climbs you can't see (other people's drafts) return a 404, and climbs in a competition, which are scored on the competition's scorecard, a 422.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [Send (full)](#send-full)
>

### `GET /api/v1/wall_photos/:id`

> Returns a wall photo: a photo of a gym wall that climbs are set on. Re-photographing a wall gives it a new current photo; climbs set on the old one keep it.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the wall photo to retrieve. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Public.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [WallPhoto](#wallphoto)
> 

### `GET /api/v1/wall_photos/:id/holds`

> Returns the holds on a wall photo. Hold masks are in the photo's `width` x `height` pixels, and each hold's `id` matches the holds of climbs set on this photo.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the wall photo whose holds you want to retrieve. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Public.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [WallPhoto (with_holds)](#wallphoto-with_holds)
> 

### `GET /api/v1/wall_photos/:id/hold_mapping`

> Returns which hold of a wall photo is which hold of the wall's previous photo. When a wall is re-photographed, Crux matches the old photo's holds to the new one's, so you can carry anything you keep per hold over to the new hold IDs. Follow a wall's photos with `previous_photo_id` and `next_photo_id`, calling this for each. Responds 404 when the photo wasn't matched to a previous photo.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the wall photo (the newer of the two). This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Public.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [HoldMapping](#holdmapping)
> 

### `POST /api/v1/webhook_registrations`

> Registers a webhook owned by you. Without `gym_slug` it gets your own events (user events: `climb.sent`, `climb.created`, `climb.viewed`). With `gym_slug` it gets that gym's events (gym events: `climb.created`, `climb.updated`, `climb.activated`, `climb.deactivated`, `climb.sent`, `gym_wall.created`), only those you could see in the app (not other climbers' draft climbs, or sends by climbers who hide their profile). It's listed with your webhooks, not the gym's. Send the parameters as a JSON body or form fields. Returns the new registration, including its `signing_secret`, with a 201 status. Returns a 422 with the reason if the URL or event type isn't valid.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `url`
> 
> The http or https URL Crux POSTs each event to. It must be on the public internet. This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `event_type`
> 
> The event to subscribe to, for example `climb.activated`. Must be a user event without `gym_slug`, or a gym event with it. This parameter is required.
> 
> ##### `gym_slug`
> 
> The URL slug of a gym to get that gym's events. You must have opened the gym in Crux (or be one of its admins), and be allowed to see it if it's private. Leave it out to get your own events. This parameter is optional.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Any authenticated user. A gym webhook's gym must be one you've opened in Crux or administer.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [WebhookRegistration (full)](#webhookregistration-full)
> 

### `DELETE /api/v1/webhook_registrations/:id`

> Deletes a webhook registration, so its URL gets no more events. Works for your own webhooks and, for gym admins, the gym's webhooks. Returns HTTP 200 if successful.
> 
> #### Parameters:
> 
> ##### `id`
> 
> The ID of the webhook registration to delete. This parameter is required.
> 
> #### Authorization:
> 
> Your own webhook registrations, or the webhook registrations of a gym you administer.
> 
> #### Response:
> 
> [Empty](#empty)
>

## Response Objects

These are the definitions of the objects returned by the API. Some objects have variants, for example, User has an "authenticated" variant with additional information that we return when you're fetching your own user. The API documentation above indicates when a variant is returned.

<!-- BEGIN AUTOGENERATED API RESPONSE OBJECTS -->

### ClimbAngleGrade

> #### `angle` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> An angle the climb's wall can be set to, in positive degrees past vertical: 0 is vertical, 40 is a 40° overhang.
>
> #### `grade` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The climb's grade at this angle, one of the gym's grades. At the climb's set `angle` it's the climb's `grade`. Null when the climb hasn't been graded at this angle.
>

### Climb

> #### `id` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> An ID that uniquely identifies the resource across Crux.
>
> #### `angle` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The wall angle this climb was set (and graded) at, in positive degrees past vertical: 0 is vertical, 40 is a 40° overhang. The climb can be climbed at any of its wall's `angles`; `grades_by_angle` has its grade at each. Only meaningful for climbs on walls with an adjustable angle; null when the climb wasn't set at an angle.
>
> #### `color` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The color of the climb. Only for official climbs in commercial gyms.
>
> #### `created_at` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> When the climb was created.
>
> #### `description` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> Optional climber-provided description of the climb.
>
> #### `foot_rules` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> Foot rules for the climb. One of [feet_follow_hands, any_feet, campus, feet_follow_hands_open_kicker, only_marked_feet], or custom_&lt;id&gt; for a feet rule the gym defined itself.
>
> #### `foot_rules_name` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> Human-readable name of the climb's foot rules, e.g. "Feet follow hands" or the name of the gym's own feet rule.
>
> #### `grade` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The grade of the climb. This will be one of the gym's available grades.
>
> #### `grades_by_angle` <span class="object-type">array [ClimbAngleGrade](#climbanglegrade)</span>
>
> The climb's grade at each angle its wall can be set to, shallowest first. Angles are in positive degrees past vertical (0 is vertical); the set `angle` is included, with the climb's `grade`, and the grade is null at angles where the climb hasn't been graded. Only for climbs on walls with an adjustable angle; empty for other climbs.
>
> #### `image_height` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> Height of the climb's image in pixels (after cropping).
>
> #### `image_url` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The final (edited) image URL for the climb: the photo with its holds highlighted. For most climbs this image is drawn from the climb's data when it's first requested, so the first request can take up to a second; after that it's cached. The URL changes whenever the climb's holds, photo or styling change.
>
> #### `image_width` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> Width of the climb's image in pixels (after cropping).
>
> #### `name` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> The name of the climb.
>
> #### `no_matching` <span class="object-type">boolean</span>
>
> Whether the climb is "no matching": hands can't match on any hold except the start and finish holds.
>
> #### `number_of_comments` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> The number of comments on this climb.
>
> #### `number_of_sends` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> The number of times this climb has been sent.
>
> #### `unedited_image_url` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The original uploaded image URL, before hold highlights.
>
> #### `unset_at` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> When the climb was marked as unset (removed from the wall).
>
> #### `updated_at` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> When the climb was last updated.
>

### Climb (full)

> #### `id` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> An ID that uniquely identifies the resource across Crux.
>
> #### `angle` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The wall angle this climb was set (and graded) at, in positive degrees past vertical: 0 is vertical, 40 is a 40° overhang. The climb can be climbed at any of its wall's `angles`; `grades_by_angle` has its grade at each. Only meaningful for climbs on walls with an adjustable angle; null when the climb wasn't set at an angle.
>
> #### `color` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The color of the climb. Only for official climbs in commercial gyms.
>
> #### `created_at` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> When the climb was created.
>
> #### `description` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> Optional climber-provided description of the climb.
>
> #### `foot_rules` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> Foot rules for the climb. One of [feet_follow_hands, any_feet, campus, feet_follow_hands_open_kicker, only_marked_feet], or custom_&lt;id&gt; for a feet rule the gym defined itself.
>
> #### `foot_rules_name` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> Human-readable name of the climb's foot rules, e.g. "Feet follow hands" or the name of the gym's own feet rule.
>
> #### `grade` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The grade of the climb. This will be one of the gym's available grades.
>
> #### `grades_by_angle` <span class="object-type">array [ClimbAngleGrade](#climbanglegrade)</span>
>
> The climb's grade at each angle its wall can be set to, shallowest first. Angles are in positive degrees past vertical (0 is vertical); the set `angle` is included, with the climb's `grade`, and the grade is null at angles where the climb hasn't been graded. Only for climbs on walls with an adjustable angle; empty for other climbs.
>
> #### `gym_name` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> The name of the gym where the climb is located.
>
> #### `gym_slug` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> The URL slug of the gym where the climb is located.
>
> #### `holds` <span class="object-type">array [ClimbHold (on_climb)](#climbhold-on_climb)</span>
>
> List of holds in the climb.
>
> #### `image_height` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> Height of the climb's image in pixels (after cropping).
>
> #### `image_url` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The final (edited) image URL for the climb: the photo with its holds highlighted. For most climbs this image is drawn from the climb's data when it's first requested, so the first request can take up to a second; after that it's cached. The URL changes whenever the climb's holds, photo or styling change.
>
> #### `image_width` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> Width of the climb's image in pixels (after cropping).
>
> #### `name` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> The name of the climb.
>
> #### `no_matching` <span class="object-type">boolean</span>
>
> Whether the climb is "no matching": hands can't match on any hold except the start and finish holds.
>
> #### `number_of_comments` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> The number of comments on this climb.
>
> #### `number_of_sends` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> The number of times this climb has been sent.
>
> #### `photo` <span class="object-type">nullable object</span>
>
> The photo the climb is drawn on: `{ id, width, height }`. Its holds are at `GET /api/v1/wall_photos/:id/holds`, and the climb's `photo_mask`s are in its pixels. Null for climbs without a photo.
>
> #### `setter_id` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> User ID of the setter (custom climbs only).
>
> #### `setter_name` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> Name of the setter who posted the climb (custom climbs only).
>
> #### `unedited_image_url` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The original uploaded image URL, before hold highlights.
>
> #### `unset_at` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> When the climb was marked as unset (removed from the wall).
>
> #### `updated_at` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> When the climb was last updated.
>
> #### `wall_id` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The ID of the wall this climb is on. Returns null if the climb is not set on a wall.
>
> #### `sends` <span class="object-type">array [Send](#send)</span>
>
> List of sends for this climb.
>

Only for videos on climbs on walls with an adjustable angle; null for other comments, including every comment posted through the API (which are text only).

### ClimbDrawing

> #### `color` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The hex color code of the drawing (e.g. '#FF0000').
>
> #### `points` <span class="object-type">array</span>
>
> An array of coordinate pairs [[x, y], ...] that form the drawing path. Coordinates are relative to the climb image dimensions.
>
> #### `type` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> The type of drawing modification. Always 'draw'.
>

### ClimbHold

> #### `id` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> Identifies the hold. A hold has the same ID in a wall's or photo's holds and in the holds of every climb that uses it, so you can match them up (to light LEDs, for example). Re-photographing a wall gives its holds new IDs.
>
> #### `mask` <span class="object-type">array</span>
>
> The outline of the hold: a list of [x, y] points that form a polygon. In a photo's holds, the points are in the photo's `width` x `height` pixels. In a wall's `holds`, they're in the wall's `image_width` x `image_height` pixels. In a climb's holds, they're in the pixels of the image the climb was marked up on, before cropping; use `photo_mask` instead.
>

### ClimbHold (on_climb)

> #### `circuit_numbers` <span class="object-type">array</span>
>
> Circuit identifiers applied to this hold. Empty when the climb is not part of a circuit.
>
> #### `hold_type` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> The type of hold. One of [hand, hand_l, hand_r, foot, foot_l, foot_r, start, finish, zone]
>
> #### `id` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> Identifies the hold. A hold has the same ID in a wall's or photo's holds and in the holds of every climb that uses it, so you can match them up (to light LEDs, for example). Re-photographing a wall gives its holds new IDs.
>
> #### `mask` <span class="object-type">array</span>
>
> The outline of the hold: a list of [x, y] points that form a polygon. In a photo's holds, the points are in the photo's `width` x `height` pixels. In a wall's `holds`, they're in the wall's `image_width` x `image_height` pixels. In a climb's holds, they're in the pixels of the image the climb was marked up on, before cropping; use `photo_mask` instead.
>
> #### `photo_mask` <span class="object-type">nullable array</span>
>
> The outline of the hold in the pixels of the climb's `photo` (`width` x `height`), the same as in the photo's holds. Null if the climb has no photo.
>

### GymWall

> #### `id` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> An ID that uniquely identifies the resource across Crux.
>
> #### `angle_adjustable` <span class="object-type">boolean</span>
>
> Whether the wall's angle can be adjusted (for example a board on a hinge). An adjustable wall supports the angles in `angles`, and its climbs can be climbed at any of them.
>
> #### `angles` <span class="object-type">array integer</span>
>
> The angles the wall can be set to, in positive degrees past vertical (0 is vertical, 40 is a 40° overhang), shallowest first. `minimum_angle` and `maximum_angle` are the first and last. Its climbs can be climbed, sent and graded at each of these angles. Empty when `angle_adjustable` is false.
>
> #### `created_at` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> Timestamp when the wall was created.
>
> #### `current_photo` <span class="object-type">nullable [WallPhoto](#wallphoto)</span>
>
> The wall's current photo, which new climbs are set on. Its holds are at `GET /api/v1/gym_walls/:id/holds`. Null if the wall has no photo.
>
> #### `holds` <span class="object-type">array nullable [ClimbHold](#climbhold)</span>
>
> Deprecated: use `GET /api/v1/gym_walls/:id/holds`, which returns the same holds without including them in every wall. List of predicted holds on the wall.
>
> #### `image_height` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The height of the wall image in pixels.
>
> #### `image_url` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The URL of the wall's image.
>
> #### `image_width` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The width of the wall image in pixels.
>
> #### `maximum_angle` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The highest angle the wall can be set to, in positive degrees past vertical: 0 is vertical, 40 is a 40° overhang. Only meaningful when `angle_adjustable` is true; null when no range is set.
>
> #### `minimum_angle` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The lowest angle the wall can be set to, in positive degrees past vertical: 0 is vertical, 40 is a 40° overhang. Only meaningful when `angle_adjustable` is true; null when no range is set.
>
> #### `name` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> The name of the wall.
>
> #### `updated_at` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> Timestamp when the wall was last updated.
>

### HoldMapping

> #### `carried_forward` <span class="object-type">boolean</span>
>
> Whether Crux treats the matched holds as the same holds (enough of them matched): their usage carries over to this photo. The matches are returned either way.
>
> #### `computed_at` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> When the holds were matched. Editing either photo's holds matches them again.
>
> #### `holds` <span class="object-type">array [HoldMappingHold](#holdmappinghold)</span>
>
> Every hold on this photo, with the ID of the same hold on the previous photo when it was matched, or of the hold it replaced when it was swapped for it.
>
> #### `match_rate` <span class="object-type">number</span>
>
> How many of the holds matched, from 0 to 1: the matched holds divided by the hold count of whichever photo has fewer. A low rate usually means the wall was reset.
>
> #### `photo_id` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> The wall photo.
>
> #### `previous_photo_id` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> The wall's photo before this one, whose holds these are matched to.
>
> #### `removed_hold_ids` <span class="object-type">array</span>
>
> IDs of holds on the previous photo that weren't matched to any hold on this one (removed, swapped for a different hold, or not recognised).
>

### HoldMappingHold

> #### `id` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> The hold's ID on this photo, as in the photo's holds.
>
> #### `previous_id` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> The same hold's ID on the previous photo. Null when the hold wasn't matched to one there (it's new, or wasn't recognised).
>
> #### `swapped_from_id` <span class="object-type">nullable string</span>
>
> When this hold replaced a different hold of similar shape in the same spot on the previous photo (for example a hold of another colour), that hold's ID on the previous photo. The two aren't matched, so previous_id is null. Null otherwise.
>

### Send

> #### `id` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> An ID that uniquely identifies the resource across Crux.
>
> #### `angle` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The angle the climb was climbed at, in positive degrees past vertical: 0 is vertical, 40 is a 40° overhang. One of the climb's wall's `angles`. Only for climbs on walls with an adjustable angle; null for other climbs.
>
> #### `attempts` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> How many attempts the send took, as the climber logged it (a flash is 1). Null when they didn't log it, which includes every repeat send from before repeats' attempts could be logged (November 2026).
>
> #### `created_at` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> Timestamp when the send was recorded.
>
> #### `repeat` <span class="object-type">boolean</span>
>
> Whether this was a repeat send of the climb. On a wall with an adjustable angle, a send is a repeat only when the climber has already sent the climb at the same `angle`.
>
> #### `send_date` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> The date of the session in which this send occurred.
>
> #### `user` <span class="object-type">[User](#user)</span>
>
> The user who sent the climb.
>

### WallPhoto

> #### `id` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> An ID that uniquely identifies the resource across Crux.
>
> #### `created_at` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> Timestamp when the photo was first used on Crux.
>
> #### `current` <span class="object-type">boolean</span>
>
> Whether this is the wall's current photo. When a wall is re-photographed, its old photo stays (climbs set on it are still drawn on it) but is no longer current.
>
> #### `height` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> The height of the photo in pixels. Hold masks on this photo are in these pixels.
>
> #### `holds_carried_forward` <span class="object-type">nullable boolean</span>
>
> Whether Crux treats this photo's holds as the same holds as on `previous_photo_id` (enough of them matched): their usage carries over, and climbs set on the previous photo count on the holds they match here. Null without a previous photo.
>
> #### `image_url` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>
> The URL of the photo. The image may be smaller than `width` x `height`, but it has the same shape, so scale hold masks by the image's width divided by `width`.
>
> #### `match_rate` <span class="object-type">nullable number</span>
>
> How many of the holds matched between `previous_photo_id` and this photo, from 0 to 1: the matched holds divided by the hold count of whichever photo has fewer. A low rate usually means the wall was reset. Null without a previous photo.
>
> #### `next_photo_id` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The photo that replaced this one on the wall, when Crux has matched this photo's holds to it. Null if there is none.
>
> #### `previous_photo_id` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The wall's photo before this one, when Crux has matched its holds to this photo's (see `GET /api/v1/wall_photos/:id/hold_mapping`). Follow it back to see the wall's earlier photos. Null if there is none.
>
> #### `wall_id` <span class="object-type">nullable integer</span>
>
> The ID of the gym wall this is a photo of. Null for photos posted for climbs at the gym without picking a wall.
>
> #### `width` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> The width of the photo in pixels. Hold masks on this photo are in these pixels.
>

### WebhookDelivery

> #### `id` <span class="object-type">integer</span>
>
> An ID that uniquely identifies the resource across Crux.
>
> #### `created_at` <span class="object-type">string</span>
>

> The secret this registration's deliveries are signed with.
